Use case: identity-preserve. Project asset: photorealistic historical film still, one coherent 16:9 landscape frame, no collage, no text. Identity fidelity is higher priority than continuity, acting, and beautification. The primary identity masters override every scene/pose image. Keep real skin texture, adult maturity, original facial ratios; do not idealize into generic costume-drama leads. Preserve the established pale blue floral/ivory robe and jade hairpin for Pan Hui and navy robe/ivory collar/brown sash/high bun for Sun. Pan Hui must retain the reference's horizontally long, relatively narrow almond eyes and subtly upturned outer corners, eyebrow shape and brow-eye distance, exact nose width/length/tip, original lip shape and subtly upturned corners, jaw/chin length to face width. Her small beauty mole stays on the skin below the mouth corner at image-right in a frontal view, with the same gap, size and relative position. Do not mirror. No round enlarged eyes, no childlike or pleading expression, no cosmetic-surgery or influencer face. Sunset light comes from back-right. No other people, no invented scenery or wardrobe.
Image 1 is the sole Pan Hui identity master. Image 2 is ONLY pine/meadow/sunset environment. Create the key moment after Pan Hui recognizes Sun singing off screen toward image-left: she has just finished turning, camera beside Sun sees her NEAR FRONTAL face (0 to 5 degrees), upper body and waist, in focus. She looks just left of camera at him, not at the viewer. The long narrow almond eyes soften with real amusement first, then the distinctive corners of her lips lift into a clearly visible, warm, restrained, familiar, slightly coquettish smile. Show a real smile, not a blank serious gaze; she is silently listening, not singing. Do not widen eyes or make a sweet innocent girl. Huge pine trunk softly present behind at screen-right, warm meadow and distant mountains; subtle rim light and breeze, natural skin color. Facial identity must look like the unchanged first reference person. No exaggerated head turn or side profile. The reference face is the target, not a prettier replacement.
